text: Track 8.1 I want to drive into London next week. My brother lives there, but I read that I have to pay a congestion charge. What's that? That's the money you have to pay to drive into the centre of the city on weekdays. Why don't you take the metro or a bus into the centre? There's a lot of traffic in London and there are bus lanes everywhere. Are they the parts of the road only for buses? Yes and no. They help the buses move around the city faster, but taxis and motorbikes can also go in them. However, cars are not allowed during the day. The passengers think bus lanes are a good idea because their journeys are much quicker, but don't drive in a bus lane or you'll get a fine. What's a fine? It's money you pay when you do something wrong. It's about £80, but you only pay £40 if you pay in two weeks. Oh no, I don't think I want to drive into London. Most people travel by public transport. Is it expensive? The metro fairs are cheap. The fair means the price of the ticket. So how much is it? When are you going? Tuesday morning. Don't go at peak time. That's the time when a lot of people travel. Well, I have to leave at 8.30. Where does your brother live? He lives in central London. That's zone one, so you certainly don't want to drive into the centre. Park your car in the suburbs and then take the metro. The suburbs, what are they? Oh, the suburbs are areas outside the city or town centre. That's where most people live. Drive your car to a metro station. Park and take the train. It's much easier. OK, I'll do that.
